name: The MPA Guide: stages and levels of protection
summary: Describe every marine protected area by its stage of establishment and its level of protection (fully, highly, lightly or minimally protected), so that a 'paper park' and a no-take reserve are never counted as the same thing.
how: Classify the MPA's stage: proposed, designated, implemented or actively managed.
Classify its level of protection from the activities allowed inside.
Report both alongside area, so targets count protection, not just lines on a map.
worked_in: Adopted by MPAtlas and widely used in 30x30 reporting
limits: Classifies rules on paper; outcomes still need monitoring.

evidence.citation: Grorud-Colvert, K. et al. (2021). The MPA Guide: A framework to achieve global goals for the ocean. Science 373, eabf0861.

name: Publish blue carbon soil data disaggregated, core by core
summary: Publish every soil core (depth series, dry bulk density, organic carbon, dating) rather than a site average, with standard vocabulary, so stocks can be rechecked and national averages corrected.
how: Collect cores to at least 1 m where possible.
Publish disaggregated data with methods and a DOI.
Contribute to the Coastal Carbon Network Data Library.
worked_in: Coastal Carbon Network: about 15,000 cores from every continent except Antarctica
limits: Mangrove and seagrass cores, and burial rates, remain under-represented, especially outside the US.

evidence.citation: Holmquist, J.R. et al. (2024). The Coastal Carbon Library and Atlas: Open source soil data and tools supporting blue carbon research and policy. Global Change Biology 30, e17098.

name: Grazing exclusion plots to separate grazing from water-quality loss in seagrass
summary: Fence small plots of seagrass from grazers and compare them with open plots, to tell whether a meadow is being lost to grazing or to water quality before deciding how to protect it.
how: Set paired caged and open plots at permanent monitoring sites.
Track shoot density, leaf size and canopy over at least a year.
Combine with water-quality and stable-isotope indicators.
worked_in: Bermuda Platform: caged Thalassia plots recovered while grazed plots declined
limits: A diagnostic, not a management answer: green turtles are themselves protected, and any intervention must be weighed for both.

evidence.citation: Fourqurean, J.W. et al. (2010). Effects of excluding sea turtle herbivores from a seagrass bed. Marine Ecology Progress Series 419, 223-232.
